title: Converse of Corresponding Angles Postulate
text: State the Converse of the Corresponding Angles Postulate and explain how it is used to establish that two lines are parallel.
formula: \text{If corresponding angles are equal } (\angle 1 = \angle 5) \implies L_1 \parallel L_2
options: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that corresponding angles are congruent, then the two lines are parallel.
If two lines are parallel, then their corresponding angles are complementary.
If two lines are cut by a transversal, then alternate interior angles sum to 180°.
If two lines intersect at a right angle, then their corresponding angles are equal.
answer: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that corresponding angles are congruent, then the two lines are parallel.
hint: The converse swaps the hypothesis (equal corresponding angles) and conclusion (parallel lines).
steps: **Step 1: Identify statement** - The postulate states parallel lines imply equal corresponding angles.
**Step 2: Reverse condition** - The converse states if corresponding angles are equal, the lines are parallel.
**Final Verified Answer:** \(If two lines are cut by a transversal so that corresponding angles are congruent, then the two lines are parallel.\)

title: Converse of Alternate Interior Angles Theorem
text: State the Converse of the Alternate Interior Angles Theorem.
formula: \text{If alternate interior angles are equal } (\angle 3 = \angle 6) \implies L_1 \parallel L_2
options: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.
If two lines are parallel, then alternate interior angles are supplementary.
If two lines intersect, then alternate interior angles are equal.
If consecutive interior angles are congruent, then the lines are perpendicular.
answer: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.
hint: Congruent alternate interior angles guarantee parallel lines.
steps: **Step 1: Recall theorem** - Parallel lines produce equal alternate interior angles.
**Step 2: State converse** - Equal alternate interior angles imply parallel lines.
**Final Verified Answer:** \(If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.\)

title: Converse of Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem
text: State the Converse of the Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem.
formula: \text{If consecutive interior angles are supplementary } (\angle 3 + \angle 5 = 180^\circ) \implies L_1 \parallel L_2
options: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that consecutive interior angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.
If two lines are parallel, then consecutive interior angles are equal.
If consecutive interior angles are complementary, then lines are parallel.
If two lines are cut by a transversal, alternate exterior angles sum to 180°.
answer: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that consecutive interior angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.
hint: Consecutive interior (same-side interior) angles must add up to 180° to guarantee parallel lines.
steps: **Step 1: Define consecutive interior angles** - Angles on the same side inside the parallel lines.
**Step 2: Apply condition** - Their sum must equal 180° to prove parallelism.
**Final Verified Answer:** \(If two lines are cut by a transversal so that consecutive interior angles are supplementary, then the lines are parallel.\)

title: Converse of Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem
text: State the Converse of the Alternate Exterior Angles Theorem.
formula: \text{If alternate exterior angles are equal } (\angle 1 = \angle 8) \implies L_1 \parallel L_2
options: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate exterior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.
If two lines are parallel, then alternate exterior angles are supplementary.
If alternate exterior angles are complementary, then the lines are perpendicular.
If corresponding angles sum to 180°, then the lines are parallel.
answer: If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate exterior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.
hint: Equal alternate exterior angles mean the lines cut by the transversal do not intersect.
steps: **Step 1: Identify alternate exterior angles** - Angles outside the lines on opposite sides of transversal.
**Step 2: Apply converse** - Congruence proves lines are parallel.
**Final Verified Answer:** \(If two lines are cut by a transversal so that alternate exterior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.\)

text: Find the coordinates of the orthocenter (intersection of altitudes) of triangle ABC with vertices A(0, 0), B(6, 0), and C(2, 4).

title: Laser Reflection off Mirror Line
text: A laser beam emitted from P(2, 8) reflects off a mirror line \(y = 2x - 1\) perpendicularly. Find the coordinates of the point of reflection on the mirror line.
formula: m_{\text{mirror}} = 2 \implies m_{\text{perpendicular}} = -\frac{1}{2} \implies y - 8 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 2) \implies y = -0.5x + 9 \implies 2x - 1 = -0.5x + 9 \implies 2.5x = 10 \implies x = 4, y = 7 \implies (4, 7)
